terms.gloss: the other (of two); repeated, the one … the other
terms.grammar: adjective and pronoun; gen. alterīus, dat. alterī
evidence: Cic. Att. 6.1.12: alter … frēnīs eget, alter calcāribus
Petr. 31.3: in alterā parte albās, in alterā nigrās
terms.comment: The other of a pair: alterā manū, with the other hand. Repeated, alter … alter, the one … the other. Of more than two, the others are cēterī (see the others).

phrases.latin: Cicerōnēs puerī amant inter sē, exercentur, sed discunt, alter … frēnīs eget, alter calcāribus
phrases.english: the two Cicero boys are fond of each other, they take their exercise, and they learn too, but the one needs the reins, the other the spurs

phrases.latin: olīvās in alterā parte albās, in alterā nigrās
phrases.english: olives, white on one side, black on the other

phrases.latin: ūnā manū suā faciēbat opus, et alterā tenēbat gladium
phrases.english: with one hand he did the work, and with the other he held a sword

phrases.latin: ex duābus paenulīs altera strāgulum, altera opertōrium facta est
phrases.english: of my two cloaks, one has become the rug and the other the blanket

phrases.latin: quid dem? quid nōn dem? renuis quod tū, jubet alter
phrases.english: what am I to serve? what not? what you refuse, the other orders

sources: Lewis & Short: alter
